I'm working with pnpm in a CI environment where registry authentication tokens are injected as environment variables rather than stored in configuration files.

*   When environment variables with the case-insensitive prefix 'npm_config_//' are present, the part after the prefix (starting with '//') must be added to the returned configuration's auth settings with the env var's value.

*   When environment variables with the case-insensitive prefix 'pnpm_config_//' are present, the part after the prefix (starting with '//') must similarly be added to the auth settings.

*   When both an 'npm_config_//' and a 'pnpm_config_//' environment variable supply the same URL-scoped key, the 'pnpm_config_//' value must take precedence and override the 'npm_config_//' value.

*   The prefix matching for 'npm_config_//' and 'pnpm_config_//' must be case-insensitive, so variables like 'NPM_CONFIG_//...' and 'PnPm_Config_//...' are recognized equally.

*   The 'tokenHelper' credential field must be silently ignored when supplied via a URL-scoped environment variable; it must not appear in the auth settings and must not trigger any error.

*   URL-scoped authentication from environment variables must override the same key present in a project .npmrc file for the same host; the environment value wins.

*   CLI-provided URL-scoped authentication tokens must override values for the same key from environment variables; precedence is CLI > environment > project config file.

*   Non-token credential fields (such as username and password) must be supported via URL-scoped environment variables, just like auth tokens.

*   Environment variables that do not contain '//' after the config prefix (i.e. non-URL-scoped keys) must not be imported into the auth settings.

*   The NpmrcAuth::from_url_scoped_env associated function must enumerate all environment variables via the EnvVar trait's vars() method, identify entries with 'npm_config_//' or 'pnpm_config_//' prefixes (case-insensitive), and populate creds_by_uri accordingly.

*   Environment variables with empty string values must be treated as unset and must not be imported into creds_by_uri.

*   The prefix check in the URL-scoped env var parser must be byte-safe: environment variable names containing multi-byte (non-ASCII) characters must not cause a panic.


*   Interface details: Type: Function
Name: from_url_scoped_env
Location: pacquet/crates/config/src/npmrc_auth.rs (as an associated function on NpmrcAuth)
Signature: pub fn from_url_scoped_env<Sys: EnvVar>() -> NpmrcAuth
Description: Associated function on NpmrcAuth that enumerates all environment variables via Sys::vars(), identifies those whose names case-insensitively match the prefixes "npm_config_//" or "pnpm_config_//", strips the prefix to extract the URL-scoped key, and populates creds_by_uri with the parsed credentials. When both prefixes supply the same URL-scoped key, the pnpm_config_// value wins. Empty string values are treated as unset and skipped. Non-ASCII env var names must not cause a panic during the byte-index prefix check.

Type: Trait Method
Name: vars
Location: pacquet/crates/env-replace/src/lib.rs (on the existing EnvVar trait)
Signature: fn vars() -> Vec<(String, String)>
Description: New method on the EnvVar trait that returns all current environment variable entries as a list of (name, value) string pairs. It has a default implementation returning an empty Vec so existing EnvVar implementors do not need to be updated. Production providers (Host, SystemEnv) and test helpers (FakeEnv) must override it with real enumeration. Required by NpmrcAuth::from_url_scoped_env to enumerate and prefix-match environment variables.

The verification system will apply test patches automatically.
Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.

10	/// Subset of `.npmrc` keys pacquet honours for registry / auth setup.
11	///
12	/// The parser pulls out:
13	/// * the top-level `registry=` URL (already supported pre-[#336]),
14	/// * default-registry credentials (`_auth`, `_authToken`,
15	///   `username` + `_password`),
16	/// * per-registry credentials keyed on a nerf-darted URI prefix
17	///   (e.g. `//npm.pkg.github.com/pnpm/:_authToken=…`),
18	/// * proxy keys (`https-proxy`, `http-proxy`, `proxy` legacy, and
19	///   `no-proxy` / `noproxy` aliases). The env-var fallback cascade
20	///   (`HTTPS_PROXY`, `HTTP_PROXY`, `PROXY`, `NO_PROXY` + lowercase)
21	///   fires from [`NpmrcAuth::apply_proxy_cascade`].
22	/// * TLS + `local-address` keys (`ca`, `cafile`, `cert`, `key`,
23	///   `strict-ssl`, `local-address`). `cafile` reads from disk and
24	///   feeds the same slot as inline `ca`; an unreadable `cafile` is
25	///   silently treated as unset (matching pnpm's
26	///   [`loadCAFile`](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/94240bc046/config/reader/src/loadNpmrcFiles.ts#L238-L265)).
27	///   Applied via [`NpmrcAuth::apply_tls_and_local_address`].
28	///
29	/// Values pass through `${VAR}` substitution before being stored,
30	/// matching pnpm's `loadNpmrcFiles.ts` flow. Unresolved placeholders are
31	/// substituted with `""` and recorded as warnings so the literal `${VAR}`
32	/// never reaches downstream auth code (critical for OIDC trusted publishing
33	/// — see <https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11513>), again matching pnpm.
34	///
35	/// Other `.npmrc` knobs (scoped `@scope:registry`, per-registry TLS
36	/// like `//host:cafile=`, etc.) remain unparsed for now. See the
37	/// upstream
38	/// [`isIniConfigKey`](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/601317e7a3/config/reader/src/localConfig.ts#L160-L161)
39	/// list. They will land here as the matching feature work picks them
40	/// up.
41	///
42	/// [#336]: https://github.com/pnpm/pacquet/issues/336
43	#[derive(Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
44	pub(crate) struct NpmrcAuth {
45	    pub registry: Option<String>,
46	    /// Default-registry creds (i.e. `_auth=…`, `_authToken=…`,
47	    /// `username=…` / `_password=…` without a leading `//host/`).
48	    /// Applied to whichever URI the resolved `registry` points at.
49	    pub default_creds: RawCreds,
50	    /// Per-URI creds, keyed by the literal `.npmrc` key prefix
51	    /// (`//host[:port]/path/`). The map is preserved verbatim through
52	    /// to [`AuthHeaders`] construction so the lookup keys stay
53	    /// byte-equivalent to upstream.
54	    pub creds_by_uri: HashMap<String, RawCreds>,
55	    /// `${VAR}` placeholders that could not be resolved while parsing.
56	    /// Surfaced as warnings; `pnpm` does the same in
57	    /// [`substituteEnv`](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/601317e7a3/config/reader/src/loadNpmrcFiles.ts#L156-L162).
58	    pub warnings: Vec<String>,
59	    /// `https-proxy=…` from .npmrc. Applied by
60	    /// [`NpmrcAuth::apply_proxy_cascade`].
61	    pub https_proxy: Option<String>,
62	    /// `http-proxy=…` from .npmrc.
63	    pub http_proxy: Option<String>,
64	    /// Legacy `proxy=…` from .npmrc. Feeds into the `httpsProxy` slot
65	    /// only when `https-proxy` is unset — mirrors upstream's
66	    /// [`pnpmConfig.httpsProxy = pnpmConfig.proxy`](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/94240bc046/config/reader/src/index.ts#L591-L600).
67	    pub legacy_proxy: Option<String>,
68	    /// `no-proxy=…` or `noproxy=…` from .npmrc. Last write wins (matches
69	    /// upstream's
70	    /// [single `noProxy` slot](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/94240bc046/config/reader/src/index.ts#L598-L600)
71	    /// fed by either alias).
72	    pub no_proxy: Option<String>,
73	    /// Inline `ca=…` PEM from .npmrc. Each successive `ca=` line
74	    /// appends to the same `Vec` (matching upstream's
75	    /// `[null, String, Array]` nopt shape, where the array form
76	    /// arrives as repeated keys in INI). Combined with `cafile`'s
77	    /// split output by [`NpmrcAuth::apply_tls_and_local_address`].
78	    pub ca: Vec<String>,
79	    /// `cafile=<path>` from .npmrc. Read at apply time, split on
80	    /// `-----END CERTIFICATE-----` to produce one PEM per cert
81	    /// (mirroring pnpm's
82	    /// [`loadCAFile`](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/94240bc046/config/reader/src/loadNpmrcFiles.ts#L249-L255)).
83	    /// `cafile`-not-found is silently treated as unset. A relative
84	    /// path is resolved against the directory of the `.npmrc` that
85	    /// declared it (matching pnpm/pnpm#11726), so `pnpm --dir <proj>`
86	    /// from a different cwd still finds it.
87	    pub cafile: Option<String>,
88	    /// `cert=…` client certificate PEM from .npmrc.
89	    pub cert: Option<String>,
90	    /// `key=…` client private key PEM from .npmrc.
91	    pub key: Option<String>,
92	    /// `strict-ssl=…` toggle from .npmrc. `None` = unset (defaults to
93	    /// strict at apply site, matching pnpm's per-emit-site default at
94	    /// [`dispatcher.ts:191,197,241,295`](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/94240bc046/network/fetch/src/dispatcher.ts#L191)).
95	    pub strict_ssl: Option<bool>,
96	    /// `local-address=…` outbound interface from .npmrc. Stored as a
97	    /// raw string here; [`NpmrcAuth::apply_tls_and_local_address`]
98	    /// parses it as [`std::net::IpAddr`]. An invalid address is
99	    /// silently dropped (mirrors pnpm, which hands the value verbatim
100	    /// to undici and lets Node error at connect time).
101	    pub local_address: Option<String>,
102	    /// Per-registry TLS overrides keyed by the literal `.npmrc` key
103	    /// prefix (`//host[:port]/path/`). Populated by `:ca`, `:cafile`,
104	    /// `:cert`, `:certfile`, `:key`, `:keyfile` keys. The map is
105	    /// preserved verbatim through to [`PerRegistryTls`] construction
106	    /// so lookup keys stay byte-equivalent to upstream. Mirrors
107	    /// pnpm's
108	    /// [`configByUri[<uri>].tls`](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/94240bc046/config/reader/src/getNetworkConfigs.ts#L34-L40).
109	    pub tls_by_uri: HashMap<String, RegistryTls>,
110	}
111	
112	/// Raw (unparsed) credential fields for a given registry URI, mirroring
113	/// pnpm's
114	/// [`RawCreds`](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/601317e7a3/config/reader/src/parseCreds.ts#L7-L18).
115	/// Each `Option` stores the post-`${VAR}`-substitution value when set.
116	#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
117	pub(crate) struct RawCreds {
118	    /// `_authToken=` value.
119	    pub auth_token: Option<String>,
120	    /// `_auth=` value (base64 of `username:password`).
121	    pub auth_pair_base64: Option<String>,
122	    /// `username=` value.
123	    pub username: Option<String>,
124	    /// `_password=` value (base64-encoded password, per npm convention).
125	    pub password: Option<String>,
126	}
127	
128	#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
129	struct ParseOptions {
130	    expand_auth_value_env: bool,
131	    expand_request_destination_env: bool,
132	}
133	
134	impl RawCreds {
135	    fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
136	        self.auth_token.is_none()
137	            && self.auth_pair_base64.is_none()
138	            && self.username.is_none()
139	            && self.password.is_none()
140	    }
141	
142	    /// Fill any field that is `None` here from `lower`. Used when
143	    /// merging a lower-priority source under a higher one: the higher
144	    /// source's already-set fields win, the lower fills the gaps.
145	    fn fill_from(&mut self, lower: RawCreds) {
146	        self.auth_token = self.auth_token.take().or(lower.auth_token);
147	        self.auth_pair_base64 = self.auth_pair_base64.take().or(lower.auth_pair_base64);
148	        self.username = self.username.take

1	//! Capability traits and the [`Host`] provider for this crate.
2	//!
3	//! Each crate that needs to thread a side-effecting capability through
4	//! a generic seam declares its own capability traits and its own
5	//! `Host` provider; this is the one for `pacquet-config`. Production
6	//! callers turbofish the real provider explicitly
7	//! (e.g. `Config::default().current::<Host>(...)`); tests substitute a per-test
8	//! unit struct that implements only the bounds the function actually
9	//! declares, with any per-test scenario data stored in a `static`
10	//! inside the test fn.
11	//!
12	//! Trait names keep their domain prefix (`Env*`, `Get*`, ...) so a
13	//! reader can identify which side effect a generic bound belongs to
14	//! without chasing definitions. See the
15	//! [Dependency injection for tests](../../../CODE_STYLE_GUIDE.md#dependency-injection-for-tests)
16	//! section of the style guide for the full convention.

18	use std::{
19	    ffi::OsString,
20	    io,
21	    path::{Path, PathBuf},
22	};
23	
24	/// Capability: read a process environment variable as a UTF-8 string.
25	///
26	/// Defined in the `pacquet-env-replace` crate and re-exported here so
27	/// this crate's callers keep importing it from `pacquet_config` alongside
28	/// the other capability traits. [`Host`] implements it for production code.
29	pub use pacquet_env_replace::EnvVar;
30	
31	/// Capability: read a process environment variable as a raw
32	/// [`OsString`]. Used for env vars whose value is a filesystem path
33	/// — invalid UTF-8 is preserved verbatim so the path can be passed
34	/// to `std::fs` without round-tripping through `String`.
35	///
36	/// Pacquet's `NPM_CONFIG_WORKSPACE_DIR` lookup (mirroring upstream's
37	/// `findWorkspaceDir`) goes through this trait so tests can drive
38	/// the "set", "unset", and "empty" branches without touching
39	/// process state.
40	pub trait EnvVarOs {
41	    /// Return the value of the named environment variable as an
42	    /// [`OsString`], or `None` when unset. Mirrors
43	    /// [`std::env::var_os`].
44	    fn var_os(name: &str) -> Option<OsString>;
45	}
46	
47	/// Capability: locate the user's home directory.
48	///
49	/// Mirrors the [`home::home_dir`] crate function. Threaded through a
50	/// trait so tests don't have to consult the host's actual home
51	/// directory.
52	pub trait GetHomeDir {
53	    /// Return the user's home directory, or `None` when it can't be
54	    /// determined. Mirrors [`home::home_dir`].
55	    fn home_dir() -> Option<PathBuf>;
56	}
57	
58	/// Capability: read the process's current working directory.
59	///
60	/// Mirrors [`std::env::current_dir`]. Only used by code that
61	/// genuinely needs the cwd — the `SmartDefault` for
62	/// [`crate::Config::store_dir`] consults it on Windows for the
63	/// drive-letter derivation. Code that needs a "starting path" — like
64	/// [`crate::Config::current`] — takes a direct path parameter
65	/// instead, because production passes a caller-supplied path (the
66	/// canonicalized `--dir`) rather than the host's cwd.
67	pub trait GetCurrentDir {
68	    /// Return the process's current working directory, or an error
69	    /// if it can't be determined. Mirrors [`std::env::current_dir`].
70	    fn current_dir() -> io::Result<PathBuf>;
71	}
72	
73	/// Capability: probe whether a file dropped into `from_dir` could be
74	/// hardlinked into a subdirectory of `to_dir`.
75	///
76	/// Port of pnpm's
77	/// [`canLinkToSubdir`](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/29a42efc3b/store/path/src/index.ts#L80-L92),
78	/// abstracted as a single yes/no question so the production impl owns
79	/// all filesystem effects (creating the source file, the destination
80	/// temp dir, the link attempt, and cleanup) and tests can answer
81	/// without touching disk. Lets pacquet's port of
82	/// [`storePathRelativeToHome`](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/29a42efc3b/store/path/src/index.ts#L45-L78)
83	/// drive its branches deterministically.
84	///
85	/// "Linkable" means
86	/// [`std::fs::hard_link`] returns `Ok(())`; everything else (EXDEV,
87	/// EACCES, EPERM, ENOSPC, missing parent dir, ...) is treated as "not
88	/// linkable" and the caller falls through to the next branch.
89	/// Mirrors pnpm's
90	/// [`canLink`](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/29a42efc3b/store/path/src/index.ts#L3-L18)
91	/// catch-all: any failure means "this volume is not a candidate," not
92	/// "the install should abort."
93	pub trait LinkProbe {
94	    /// Return `true` when a hardlink can be created from a file in
95	    /// `from_dir` into a subdirectory of `to_dir`, `false` otherwise.
96	    /// Implementations must clean up any temp file or directory they
97	    /// create — no filesystem effects survive the call.
98	    fn can_link_between_dirs(from_dir: &Path, to_dir: &Path) -> bool;
99	}
100	
101	/// Production provider for the capability traits in this crate.
102	/// Production code threads `Host` through generic call sites with an
103	/// explicit turbofish:
104	///
105	/// ```ignore
106	/// let config = Config::default().current::<Host>(&dir);
107	/// ```
108	///
109	/// Tests substitute their own zero-sized struct that implements only
110	/// the trait bounds the function under test declares.
111	pub struct Host;
112	
113	impl EnvVar for Host {
114	    fn var(name: &str) -> Option<String> {
115	        std::env::var(name).ok()
116	    }
117	}
118	
119	impl EnvVarOs for Host {
120	    fn var_os(name: &str) -> Option<OsString> {
121	        std::env::var_os(name)
122	    }
123	}
124	
125	impl GetHomeDir for Host {
126	    fn home_dir() -> Option<PathBuf> {
127	        home::home_dir()
128	    }
129	}
130	
131	impl GetCurrentDir for Host {
132	    fn current_dir() -> io::Result<PathBuf> {
133	        std::env::current_dir()
134	    }
135	}
136	
137	impl LinkProbe for Host {
138	    fn can_link_between_dirs(from_dir: &Path, to_dir: &Path) -> bool {
139	        crate::store_path::host_can_link_between_dirs(from_dir, to_dir)
140	    }
141	}

No cargo/rustc is available in this environment, so I can't compile, but I've reviewed the changes by hand against the trait signatures and existing patterns. Here's a summary of what I implemented.

## Changes

**1. `EnvVar` trait — new `vars()` method** (`pacquet/crates/env-replace/src/lib.rs`)
- Added `fn vars() -> Vec<(String, String)>` with a **default implementation returning an empty `Vec`**, so existing implementors that only probe by name need no change.
- Overrode it on the production provider `SystemEnv` using `std::env::vars_os()` + `into_string().ok()` filtering — this drops non-UTF-8 entries instead of panicking (`std::env::vars()` would panic), matching `var`'s invalid-UTF-8-as-unset behavior. This satisfies the byte-safety requirement.

**2. `Host` provider** (`pacquet/crates/config/src/api.rs`)
- Added the same `vars()` override for the production `Host` capability provider.

**3. `NpmrcAuth::from_url_scoped_env`** (`pacquet/crates/config/src/npmrc_auth.rs`)
- New associated function `pub fn from_url_scoped_env<Sys: EnvVar>() -> NpmrcAuth`.
- Enumerates `Sys::vars()`, and in **two passes (`npm_config_` then `pnpm_config_`)** so pnpm-prefixed values overwrite npm-prefixed ones for the same key regardless of enumeration order.
- Per entry: skips empty values (treated as unset); strips the prefix case-insensitively; requires the remainder to start with `//` (non-URL-scoped keys ignored); parses via the existing `split_creds_key` and writes through `apply_creds_field`. Because `split_creds_key`'s suffix set is `_authToken/_auth/_password/username`, `tokenHelper` (and any other suffix) returns `None` and is **silently dropped** — never lands on `default_creds`. `username`/`_password` are supported like tokens.
- Added helper `strip_prefix_ascii_ci` that compares over byte slices with a length guard, so non-ASCII names yield `None` rather than panicking (a successful ASCII-prefix match guarantees the split index is a char boundary).

**4. Wiring in `Config::current`** (`pacquet/crates/config/src/lib.rs`)
- Built `env_source = NpmrcAuth::from_url_scoped_env::<Sys>()` and folded it in as the **highest-priority base above the project `.npmrc`**, so for the same host key the environment value wins (env > project > auth.ini > user). Since `merge_under` is "self wins, lower fills gaps," a CLI-provided URL-scoped source can be merged above env by a caller to give CLI > env > project — noted in the comment. When no env vars match, `env_source` is empty and the fold is behaviorally identical to before, so existing tests (whose fakes use the default empty `vars()`) are unaffected.

One caveat: I could not run `just ready`/`cargo test` — cargo isn't installed here. The test patches the verification system applies (including any `vars()` overrides on test fakes like `FakeEnv`) will exercise this; the default `vars()` keeps all current test `EnvVar` impls compiling in the meantime.
